newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's "pirate of the airwaves" strikes again.
newsitem.headline: Italy's "pirate of the airwaves" strikes again.

text.p: Italy's "pirate of the airwaves," a man who interrupts broadcasts on state television to read separatist declarations, has struck for the fifth time in three weeks, officials said on Sunday.

Viewers of the movie classic "Gone With the Wind" in the northeastern town of Treviso on Saturday night heard a man with a thick Venetian accent break into the film overlaying the voice of heroine Scarlett O'Hara.

The man read a seven-minute declaration in the name of the "Most Serene Venetian Government" similar to those read on four previous occasions when broadcasts on Italy's RAI state television network were interrupted. Police are investigating.
The separatist Northern League party, which proclaimed independence for its self-styled state of Padania in Venice last year, denied that it was involved.
Venice, known as the "Serenissima" or "Most Serene", was a republic for 14 centuries but lost its independence in 1797 when the French took control.
